checks: Original 181e74b2f3c435dc §§1–2 agrees with the exact conclusion for arbitrary signed μ and nonatomic source ν. Its §3 application to a separate common-curvature stress is outside this frozen proposition.

Factoring the bounded-test functional through two moment maps needs no surjectivity. A linear functional on their image extends to ℝ². The continuous Green potential coincides with the sine and cosine combination throughout the support, since the equality is ν-almost everywhere.

For an atom at θ the kernel as a function of s has left derivative −1 and right derivative zero at θ, so the derivative jump is +1. Away from θ it solves the homogeneous equation. Boundedness justifies the test-function Fubini calculation for signed μ. The kernel is Lipschitz and the formula gives a locally BV derivative.

At a continuity point of the BV derivative that is an accumulation point of E, the derivative of the identically zero values along E vanishes. The isolated points and jump points are countable and have zero atomless derivative measure.

Vol'pert's scalar BV chain rule gives the diffuse derivative multiplier Tε′(g) and exact jump differences. Uniform convergence to zero and dominated variation convergence of the jump part leave 1_{g=0}Ddiff g as the zero measure. This includes the absolutely continuous derivative as well as the Cantor derivative. The term F ds vanishes on E.

overlap.comparison: The proof already contains the same BV chain-rule calculation for derivatives of nonnegative Jensen gaps and compact Green perturbations. The statement here turns annihilation of arbitrary bounded two-moment tests for a signed forcing into diffuse locality on a possibly singular source support.

Its Dirichlet tent Green potential treats a bounded step forcing and gives pointwise cost and endpoint identities. This candidate uses a sine Green potential and an atomless restriction of an arbitrary signed measure.

readability: Use the usual precise BV representative at continuity points. The frozen proof cites the primary chain rule, verified in §5, subsection 13.2 of [Vol'pert, The spaces BV and quasilinear equations](https://doi.org/10.1070/SM1967v002n02ABEH002340).
